model_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_id, p.product_name, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o2 JOIN order_items oi2 ON o2.order_id = oi2.order_id WHERE o2.customer_id = c.customer_id AND oi2.product_id = p.product_id) > 1;
question_used: Which products have been ordered more than once by the same customer, and what are the product ID, product name, customer ID, and customer's first and last name for each?

model_sql: SELECT c.city, AVG(order_totals.order_value) AS avg_order_value FROM customers c JOIN (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_value FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id) AS order_totals ON c.customer_id = order_totals.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC;
question_used: What is the city name and average order value per customer city?

model_sql: SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM categories c JOIN products p ON c.category_id = p.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC;
question_used: How many distinct customers ordered from each product category, listed by category name and count of distinct customers?

model_sql: SELECT w.warehouse_name, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS inventory_value FROM warehouses w JOIN inventory i ON w.warehouse_id = i.warehouse_id JOIN products p ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_name ORDER BY inventory_value DESC;
question_used: What is the total inventory value, calculated as price times quantity, for each warehouse, listed by warehouse name and inventory value?

model_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.handled_by JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Berlin' GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name ORDER BY order_count DESC;
question_used: Which employees handled orders for customers from Berlin, and how many such orders did each one handle, listed by employee ID, first name, last name, and order count?

model_sql: SELECT w.warehouse_name, MAX(i.quantity) AS max_quantity, MIN(i.quantity) AS min_quantity FROM warehouses w JOIN inventory i ON w.warehouse_id = i.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_name ORDER BY w.warehouse_name;
question_used: What are the highest and lowest stock quantities in each warehouse, listed by warehouse name, maximum quantity, and minimum quantity?

model_sql: SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS order_year, MONTH(order_date) AS order_month, status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2025 GROUP BY YEAR(order_date), MONTH(order_date), status ORDER BY order_year, order_month, order_count DESC;
question_used: How many orders of each status were placed in each month of 2025, listed by year, month, status, and order count?

model_sql: SELECT c.category_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_unit_price, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name ORDER BY avg_unit_price DESC;
question_used: Which product categories have the highest average unit price across all orders, listed by category name, average unit price, and order count, ranked from highest to lowest?

model_sql: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'cancelled');
question_used: Which customers have never placed a cancelled order, listed by customer ID, first name, and last name?

model_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_quantity_ordered FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_ordered DESC;
question_used: What is the total quantity ordered for every product, including products never ordered, listed by product ID, product name, and total quantity ordered?

model_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products) GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 1;
question_used: Considering only products priced above the average product price, which customer spent the most on them, and what is their customer ID, first name, last name, and total spend?

model_sql: SELECT d.department_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_value, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) DESC) AS dept_rank FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.handled_by JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name ORDER BY total_value DESC;
question_used: How do departments rank by the total order value handled by their employees, listed by department name, total value, and rank?

model_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(i.quantity) AS total_stock FROM products p JOIN inventory i ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM order_items) GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(i.quantity) > 0;
question_used: Which products have never been ordered but currently have stock, listed by product ID, product name, and total stock quantity?

model_sql:
SELECT 
    c.category_name, 
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, 
    (SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(oi2.quantity * oi2.unit_price) FROM order_items oi2)) AS revenue_percentage 
FROM order_items oi 
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id 
JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id 
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name 
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
question_used: What percentage of total revenue comes from each product category, listed by category name, total revenue, and revenue percentage?

model_sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_value FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.handled_by JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, o.order_id ORDER BY order_value DESC LIMIT 3;
question_used: Who handled the three highest-value orders overall, listed by employee ID, first name, last name, order ID, and order value?

model_sql:
SELECT 
    e.employee_id, 
    e.first_name, 
    e.last_name, 
    m.first_name AS manager_first_name, 
    m.last_name AS manager_last_name, 
    COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS handled_value 
FROM employees e 
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id 
LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.handled_by 
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id 
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, m.first_name, m.last_name 
ORDER BY handled_value DESC;
question_used: Who is each employee's manager, and what is the total order value each employee personally handled, listed by employee ID, first name, last name, manager's first and last name, and handled value?

model_sql:
SELECT 
    c.category_name, 
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.city = 'Berlin' THEN i.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS berlin_quantity, 
    SUM(i.quantity) AS total_quantity, 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN w.city = 'Berlin' THEN i.quantity ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(i.quantity)) AS berlin_percentage 
FROM categories c 
JOIN products p ON c.category_id = p.category_id 
JOIN inventory i ON p.product_id = i.product_id 
JOIN warehouses w ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id 
GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name 
HAVING berlin_percentage > 50.0 
ORDER BY berlin_percentage DESC;
question_used: Which product categories have more than 50 percent of their total stock located in Berlin, listed by category name, Berlin quantity, total quantity, and Berlin percentage?

model_sql:
SELECT 
    c.customer_id, 
    c.first_name, 
    c.last_name, 
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spend, 
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) DESC) AS spend_rank,
    (SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) / (SELECT SUM(oi2.quantity * oi2.unit_price) FROM order_items oi2)) * 100 AS percentage_of_total
FROM customers c

JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id 
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name 
ORDER BY total_spend DESC;
question_used: How do customers rank by total spend from highest to lowest, listed by customer ID, first name, last name, total spend, rank, and percentage of the overall total?

model_sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) AS distinct_categories, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c.category_name) AS category_names FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) > 3 ORDER BY distinct_categories DESC;
question_used: Which orders included items from more than three different product categories, listed by order ID, customer ID, number of distinct categories, and category names?

model_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') AS order_month,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_order_value
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(o.order_date, '%Y-%m')
)
SELECT 
    order_month,
    total_order_value,
    LAG(total_order_value) OVER (ORDER BY order_month) AS previous_month_order_value
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY order_month;
question_used: What is the month-over-month growth in total order value, listed by month, that month's total order value, and the previous month's total order value?
